newsitem.title: UK: Loan repayment may see cut in Brazil sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Loan repayment may see cut in Brazil sugar output.

text.p: Brazil's cash-strapped sugar industry could be forced to reduce output while it repays enormous loans but high world prices should encourage maximum efficiency, the managing director of F.O. Licht said on Friday.
"Brazil has enormous potential to produce more sugar," Helmut Ahlfeld told a London conference hosted by Agra Europe.

He cited industry sources as saying cash-strapped Brazilian millers would face difficulties repaying loans estimated at up to $5 billion, which would trigger a wave of mergers in the sugar/alcohol complex and so reduce the number of mills.
"This in turn, it is feared, could lead to a reduction in the area planted to cane of up to 25 percent over the next five to 10 years while production will shrink by 10 to 20 percent," Ahlfeld said.
"However given the fact that Brazil is a highly efficient sugar producer it is hard to imagine that Brazilian production will show the indicated decline if world market prices are right."

Ahlfeld said availability of cane should nt be a problem for sugar producers as only 35 percent of all Brazilian cane in 1995/96 was destined for sugar production, with the remainder going into the ailing alcohol sector.
